newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Private-public power partnerships seen in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Private-public power partnerships seen in Brazil.

text.p: A study of Brazil's power industry concluded that public and private sector partnerships were the most suitable way of injecting much needed private funds into the industry, given the lack of rules governing private participation in the power sector.

The study, "The New Context of Brazil's Electricity Sector" published by the private National Industry Confederation (CNI), said private investment in the government-run power sector was crucial if Brazil did not want to experience serious power shortages in the future.

"The urgency of the situation does not allow us to restructure the sector prior to the entry of private capital, which would be desirable," said the authors of the study, electrical engineers Roberto Pereira d'Araujo and Carlos Augusto Amaral Hoffman. "Therefore, the most appropriate fashion to deal with this transition period would be to establish partnerships between private capital and state-owned companies."

D'Araujo and Hoffman said this would be advantageous to both sides by reducing risks for private industry connected to changes in regulation of the power sector, and by preserving positive aspects of the current state-run system.

The authors said the integrated nature of Brazil's largely hydroelectric power sector, which was based on cooperation between all the players in the industry, needed a strong dose of regulation if this was to be preserved with the entry of private capital.
They said approximately 22 percent of electricity generated in Brazil was the result of integrated operations.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
